messages:
Cami: Quick heads-up — Platform team put up a proposal to centralize batching decisions (server-side policy) and deprecate the client-side `batch_size`/`batch_window` knobs in our SDKs. Thinking a 6-month sunset + compatibility shim. Thoughts?

Mike: I saw the doc. High level +1, we do want consistent batching for cost predictability. main concerns: rollback story and clients that rely on deterministic batching for latency.

Tara: +1 from UX. Console needs a toggle and clear telemetry to show when a request used client vs platform batching. Otherwise customers will be confused by token-latency changes.

Praveen: If we remove client knobs, we must preserve an escape hatch for edge cases (real-time low-latency use). Suggest instrumentation flag that surfaces to console and an SDK env var `REDWOOD_CLIENT_BATCHING=legacy` for emergency opt-out.

Ben: Compatibility note: semver major for TS/Go? Python had a minor earlier that broke `batch()` semantics. We should avoid unnecessary majors — prefer a migration warning + runtime shim that honors existing fields for N months.

Cami: Agreed. Proposal: 1) Grace period (6 months) where SDKs accept old config but send telemetry header `x-rw-client-batching: legacy|shim|none`. 2) Console exposes a deprecation banner and per-tenant rollout controls. 3) Plan a hard removal in 6 months with release notes and migration snippet.

Elaine: From product: we need a canary path (10% tenants) before global flip. Also add a dashboard tile that shows per-route P50/P95 latency + cost delta when switching to server batching. That will help sales/CS.

Mike: Implementation detail: SDKs should send both the legacy fields and a normalized `routing-batch-hint` header so platform can map safely. Example shim in Python:

```python
# before
client = RedwoodClient(batch_size=8, batch_window_ms=20)

# migration shim sends legacy header + normalized hint
headers = {
  'x-rw-client-batching': 'legacy',
  'x-rw-batch-hint': 'size=8;window=20ms'
}
response = client.generate(prompt, headers=headers)
```

Tara: Console UX: add a per-tenant toggle with tooltip: "Use platform-managed batching (recommended) — centralized batching optimizes cost/throughput. Use legacy only for strict latency requirements." Also include link to migration guide.

Praveen: Telemetry: let's sample 100% of deprecated-header flows for the first month, then 10% after. Add an event `client_batching_migration` with fields: sdk, version, route, hint, outcome(latency_delta,cost_delta).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: 6489002000 -> platform-batching-feature-flag (10% tenants).

Ben: On SDK release cadence: ship white-listed shim in a patch release (no breaking API), warn on startup logs for 3 months, then ship an opt-in removal as a minor with docs, finally drop in a major. Also we should add a CLI migration helper that scans code for `batch_size`/`batch_window` usages.

Cami: Action items I can pick up: 1) Draft migration KB + code snippets for py/ts/go. 2) Add telemetry spec PR for event + headers. 3) Coordinate console banner + dashboard tile with Elaine. Assigning myself. Anyone wants to pair on the telemetry PR?

Praveen: I'll pair on telemetry.

Tara: I'll take the banner copy + CTA UX (small task).

Mike: I'll review the shim implementation for Go/TS.

Elaine: I'll scope the dashboard tile and canary plan with product ops.

Cami: Great — filing tickets. New doc link: https://redwood-internal.example/df/migration/centralized-batching (WIP)

Ben: One more: add automated e2e smoke that verifies the `x-rw-client-batching` header is present for legacy clients during canary. Saves us time after rollout.

Cami: Good call — adding that to the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
